caption:
Alaska's coastlines, rivers and lakes get their depth read out of satellite imagery starting September 1st.

The air above them gets a model for the weather windows safe enough for a prescribed burn. The ground under them gets one that forecasts landslides. Coal refuse and ash get read for critical minerals. Concealed rock gets searched for ore nobody has found.

Six National Science Foundation awards to University of Alaska campuses obligate $18,647,929 down that column.

Each award's obligated dollars beside its end date, what the five models read, and the fifteen UAF headlines from August 9th to August 21st that name none of the six.

Erin Trochim's water award ends August 31st, 2027. The rock award runs to July 31st, 2036. Who pays to keep a model running after its award ends?

#AlaskaResearch #CriticalMinerals #Geohazards

first_comment:
Sources, primary first. Every dollar figure below is OBLIGATED money from the National Science Foundation award record and not total project value.

NSF award 2630206. Satellite derived bathymetry and river profiles. 50,000 obligated. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2630206

NSF award 2536745. A fire weather toolkit for controlled burning in Alaska. 1,588,147 obligated. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2536745

NSF award 2614749. Critical mineral recovery from coal refuse and ash at Anchorage. 3,824,575 obligated. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2614749

NSF award 2614751. The same project at Fairbanks. 913,037 obligated. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2614751

NSF award 2608510. GAIA, geophysical AI driven integration and assimilation. 1,772,170 obligated. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2608510

NSF award 2532372. The NSF Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine in Alaska. 10,500,000 obligated of a 15,000,000 estimated total on a ten year cooperative agreement. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2532372

Six awards and 18,647,929 obligated. Five projects, because 2614749 and 2614751 carry one title across two campuses. Three of the projects are collaborative and this total is the University of Alaska share.

University of Alaska Fairbanks news index. Fifteen headlines dated August 9th to August 21st and none names these six awards. The same index carried a separate AI headline on August 11th about rural power grids. https://www.uaf.edu/news/index.php

This page covered award 2532372 once before, on July 15th, and printed 15 million now with up to 160 million over ten years. Both readings come off the same record. 10,500,000 is what NSF has obligated, 15,000,000 is the estimated total on the award, and the 160 million was the Engines program's own milestone gated ceiling, which this deck does not print because no part of it is obligated.

Every Alaska AI decision this page tracks sits at https://alaskaaihq.com with its live deadline beside it.

Anyone working on these six is welcome to add what the record leaves out.

aftercare: Post this one on a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday between 8 and 11 a.m. Alaska time. Drafts land daily and the cadence is yours, so hold it for the next strong slot rather than posting into a Friday afternoon.
Paste the first comment block within 60 seconds of publishing. Keep every URL as plain text, because a hyperlink pasted without its raw address loses the link on LinkedIn.

Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes. If someone reads the Engine as a 15 million dollar award, the correction is that 10,500,000 is obligated and 15,000,000 is an estimated total over ten years.
Check saves and comments at 48 hours and log both. Saves are the signal that matters on a document post, and this deck was built to be kept as a ledger.
